title: NHS Highland expects a budget black hole of £79 million by the end of 2026/27
byline: Olivia Andrews, Local Democracy Reporter - olivia.andrews@hnmedia.co.uk
excerpt: The health board has put in place a recovery plan which is expected to bring the forecast overspend down to £63 million, if it is completed.
content:
NHS Highland has suffered a “significant deterioration” in its finances over just one month as its budget black hole is expected to reach £79 million by the end of the financial year.

A financial report due to be discussed at a meeting tomorrow (November 24) lays bare the health board's money troubles as of September.

The report explains that the "significant deterioration” of the body’s funds from August to September is due to the inclusion of slippage in the delivery of the value and efficiency programme.

The programme aims to deliver a three per cent finance reduction to keep up with Scottish Government targets, but the most recent financial update “no longer assumes full delivery” of the plans.

NHS Highland is expected to miss the mark by £17.8 million by the end of the financial year.

In an attempt to shore up its position the health board has put in place a recovery plan which is expected to bring the forecast overspend down to £63 million, if it is completed.

The health board's updated money troubles and subsequent plan have been submitted to the Scottish Government.

The papers state that a bail out by the government would bring the overspend down to £37 million.

The biggest overspends contributing to NHS Highlands’s financial woes are in acute services (the majority of hospital care) and health and social care services - both expected to reach around a £34 million overspend by the end of 2026/27.

NHS Highland was approached for comment.
